subject: physics_2
question_text: What are the basic blocks of a communication system?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Whether Communication Systems is still on the current Telangana second-year syllabus is UNCONFIRMED — NCERT removed this chapter in the 2023 rationalisation, but this book prints it. A lecturer's pen tick marks this question as expected. Physics hand-checked: every communication system has three basic blocks — transmitter, communication channel and receiver; the message signal enters at the transmitter, noise is added in the channel, and the receiver recovers the message at the other end.

recall_prompt: Name the three basic blocks of a communication system, in order, and say in one line what each one does.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three blocks named
lines: Every communication system is made of three
steps.margin_note: First mark. The three names in order — transmitter, then channel, then receiver.
steps.why: The three blocks are the path the message actually takes: it is prepared at one end, carried in the middle, and recovered at the other end, so the list is the system itself.
common_mistakes: Writing only transmitter and receiver. The channel between them is a block of its own, and it is where noise enters.
Naming devices (microphone, antenna) instead of the three blocks the question asks for.

recall.must_convey: That the three basic blocks are the transmitter, the communication channel and the receiver.
accept: the three blocks are transmitter, channel, receiver

steps.memory_tip: Follow the message: it is sent, it travels, it is received — transmitter, channel, receiver.

steps.label: What each block does
steps.mark_note: One line on each block's job
lines: The transmitter converts the message signal
into a form suitable for transmission.
The channel carries the signal to the
receiver; noise is added in the channel.
The receiver recovers the original message
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One job per block; say that noise enters in the channel.
steps.why: Naming the blocks alone does not show understanding; the mark is safe when each block's job is stated, and noise placed in the channel is the detail examiners look for.
common_mistakes: Saying the receiver removes all noise. The receiver recovers the message; noise added in the channel can only be reduced, not fully removed.
Putting noise at the transmitter. Noise enters mainly in the channel, between the two ends.

recall.must_convey: That the transmitter prepares the message signal for sending, the channel carries it and adds noise, and the receiver recovers the message.
accept: the transmitter prepares the signal for sending
the channel carries the signal and noise enters there
the receiver recovers the original message
reject: the three blocks are transmitter, channel, receiver

steps.memory_tip: Prepare, carry, recover — one verb for each block, in the same order as the blocks.

insider_note: The first mark is the three names in order; the second needs one job per block, with noise placed in the channel.
